transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, doctor. Thank you for seeing me. Um, I hope I'm in the right place for this... I'm a barber, and I've just been having a little bit of trouble at work lately. It's probably silly, but I've gotten to the point where I'll do almost anything to avoid using the straight razor. I'll switch clients with my coworkers, or, um, tell the customer the blade is missing, or even just hide it in the drawer so I don't have to look at it. I know it sounds unprofessional, I'm sorry. And if I absolutely can't get out of doing a hot towel shave... I'm just shaking through the whole thing. Is that... is that something you can help with?

Can you tell me what goes through your mind when you think about using the straight razor? Is it a fear of hurting someone, or does the thought of using the blade itself just feel unbearable for another reason?

Um, yeah, you kind of hit the nail on the head. I mean, I know it’s just a tool, right? Like, I went to school for this, I trained with it... and I can use clippers and shears all day long without batting an eye. But... I don't know, I guess my mind just goes to the worst-case scenario. 

When that straight razor is just sitting open at my station, it just... it feels like I’m about to hurt somebody. Or, or like I'm going to slip and cut myself really badly. I know it sounds completely ridiculous for a barber to say that, and I'm really sorry if it sounds like I'm just bad at my job. Does that make sense, though? Is it okay that I'm feeling that way?
When you're faced with using the straight razor, do you ever experience symptoms like a racing heart, sweating, trembling, or a feeling like you're going to faint or lose control?

Um, well... I guess I do get a little worked up. I mean, it's not like I'm completely losing control or anything dramatic like that, I promise. I try really hard to keep it together so the client doesn't notice. But... yeah, the second I hear someone ask for a hot towel shave, or if I just see the blade flipped open on the counter, it's like... my chest just tightens up right away. 

And my hands do get pretty sweaty, which isn't great when you're supposed to be holding something sharp, you know? It's almost like my body just physically wants to back away from the chair before my brain even catches up. I really try not to let it show, though. I hope that doesn't make me sound too unstable... is it normal to react physically like that?
Do you find yourself avoiding the straight razor even when you're not at work, like if you're at home or in another setting where you might need to use it?

Um, well... I guess I don't really use one at home anyway. I mean, most guys just use a regular cartridge razor or an electric trimmer for their own face, right? So it's not like I'm going out of my way to avoid it in my personal life, I promise. 

If I'm at the store and I walk down the shaving aisle, I might, you know, just kind of look the other way if I see the straight blades. But it's not like I run out of the store or anything! I just... prefer not to think about them if I don't have to. I hope that's an okay answer? I just really don't have much of a reason to be around them outside of the shop.

Can you tell me if you experience similar feelings of anxiety or physical symptoms in other situations, like when you're interacting with customers or giving presentations at work, or maybe when you're in social situations outside of work?

Um, no, not really. I mean, I actually really love talking to my clients! That's kind of the best part of being a barber, honestly. I'm totally fine chatting with people in the chair, and I don't get nervous around my friends or anything like that. 

I really try to be a good people person, you know? It's literally just the straight razor that gets to me. Everything else at work is totally fine, I promise. I don't have any issues with social stuff or talking in front of people. I hope that makes sense? I just want to make sure I'm answering your questions right.
How long have you been feeling this way about the straight razor? Has this been going on for several months, or did it start more recently?

Um, let me think... it's been going on for about 11 months now, I guess. I almost feel bad bringing this part up, because I really don't want you to think I'm a difficult employee or a complainer or anything like that. I always try to get along with everyone at the shop, I promise! 

But... well, it started right around the time the shop owner and I started having some, um, disagreements. He really wanted to push this new straight-razor shave package for the clients, and we kind of got into a few arguments over it. It wasn't anything crazy, just some tension, you know? I really try to avoid conflict. But ever since those disagreements started, I've just had this... issue with the razors. 

I hope it's okay that I mentioned the arguments? I just want to make sure I'm giving you all the right details and answering your questions properly.
Can you recall if your fear of the straight razor began suddenly after a specific incident, or if it built up gradually without a clear reason?

Um, well... I don't think there was one big, dramatic moment or anything. Like, I've never cut a client or had a bad accident with one, I promise! I'm always super careful with my tools, and I take my job really seriously. 

It just sort of... built up gradually, I guess? The more the owner and I had those little disagreements about the shave packages, the more I just started dreading the razors themselves. It wasn't like a light switch flipped one day. It just kind of crept up on me until I couldn't really handle holding them anymore. 

I hope that makes sense? I wish I could give you a better reason, like a clear starting point, so it would be easier for you to figure out. I really am trying to give you the best answers I can... am I explaining that okay?
When you know in advance that you might need to use the straight razor later, like at the start of your workday, do you feel anxious or have physical symptoms even before you see the blade?

Um, you know... I don't really get worked up beforehand. Like, I don't wake up in the morning dreading going to work or anything. I really do love my job, and I'm always happy to go in and see my clients! 

It's really only when I actually have to pick up the razor or when I'm looking right at it that I start to feel... you know, that tightness in my chest and the shaking. If I just know it's on the schedule for later in the day, I can usually keep it out of my mind and just focus on the haircuts. I try really hard to just stay positive and do a good job with the rest of my work. 

I hope that's the kind of information you were looking for? I just want to make sure I'm giving you a clear picture of how it happens. Am I doing okay with these questions?
When you think about possibly needing to use the straight razor later in the day, even if it’s not in front of you, do you ever feel anxious or have physical symptoms just from thinking about it?

Um, well, like I was saying just a minute ago... I don't really get anxious just thinking about it. I promise I'm not sitting there worrying all day! I really try to just focus on doing a good job for my clients. 

So, no, if it's just on the schedule for later, I don't get the shaking or the chest tightness or anything. It's really only when it's right there in front of me that I have a hard time. I hope it's okay that I'm repeating myself a little bit? I just want to make sure I'm answering exactly what you're asking. Did I explain that right?

Do you ever feel anxious or notice physical symptoms, like a tight chest or sweating, when you know you might have to use the straight razor later in the day, even if it's not right in front of you at that moment?

Um, I know you just asked about this, and I really hope I'm not being difficult or confusing you... but yeah, like I mentioned, I don't really get those symptoms just from knowing it's coming up later. 

I don't get the sweating or the tight chest unless I'm actually holding it or looking right at it. I'm really sorry if I'm not giving you the answer you're looking for! I just want to be totally honest so you can help me. I promise I'm not trying to be stubborn about it. Does that make sense, or am I completely misunderstanding the question?

When you're thinking about possibly needing to use the straight razor later in the day, even if it's not in front of you, do you ever start to feel anxious or notice any physical symptoms like a tight chest or sweating just from imagining it?

I... um, I really don't want to sound like a broken record, I'm so sorry. I know you're trying to be thorough, and I appreciate that so much. You're doing a great job asking all these things. 

But, um, yeah, it's still just like I was saying before. Just thinking about it or imagining it doesn't really trigger anything for me. I can picture the razor in my head right now and I feel totally fine, no tight chest or sweating at all. I really hope it's okay that my answer is still the same? I'm trying my absolute best to give you what you need... I really am.
When you imagine yourself using the straight razor, even just picturing it in your mind, do you ever feel anxious or notice any physical symptoms like a tight chest or sweating?

Oh, gosh, I... I really don't mean to be frustrating, I promise. You're being so patient with me, and I know you're just making sure you have all the details right. I hope I'm not making your job harder by saying the same thing again!

But, um, yeah, just picturing it in my mind doesn't do it. I can imagine holding it right now, and my chest feels completely normal, no sweating or anything. It's really just the physical object being right there that gets me. Is that... is that normal? I hope I'm giving you the right kind of answers. I really want to be a good patient for you.

My symptom profile covers immediate fear/anxiety response (S063) when exposed to the object, but does not include symptoms of anticipatory anxiety or fear from merely imagining the object. Therefore, there is no corresponding item in the profile.

patient.answer:
Oh, gosh, I... I really don't mean to be frustrating, I promise. You're being so patient with me, and I know you're just making sure you have all the details right. I hope I'm not making your job harder by saying the same thing again!

But, um, yeah, just picturing it in my mind doesn't do it. I can imagine holding it right now, and my chest feels completely normal, no sweating or anything. It's really just the physical object being right there that gets me. Is that... is that normal? I hope I'm giving you the right kind of answers. I really want to be a good patient for you.

inference.note: The patient's fear and avoidance are specific to the straight razor and do not generalize to other situations or objects. The anxiety is not anticipatory (i.e., does not occur when merely thinking about or imagining the razor), which rules out other anxiety disorders such as generalized anxiety or panic disorder. The specific phobia (F40.290) diagnosis fits best given the persistent, irrational fear of a specific object (straight razor) that results in marked avoidance and distress upon exposure.

opening_question.intent: Identify the patient's primary concern or reason for seeking psychiatric evaluation
opening_question.question: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with a specific phobia related to the use of straight razors, characterized by marked fear when confronted with the object, avoidance behavior, and somatic symptoms upon direct exposure. The fear is circumscribed to the straight razor and does not generalize to other situations or objects. The duration has exceeded 6 months, and the response is not better explained by another anxiety disorder.
